story_type: two kayakers caught in a gale, basket hoists through wind and whitecaps
hook: Two kayakers caught in 60 knot winds.
narration: Two kayakers were caught in eight foot swells and winds up to sixty knots.
It happened in Bellingham Bay, Washington, in December.
One of them had packed a handheld radio in his kayak for exactly this kind of emergency, and he used it to call for help.
A Coast Guard helicopter crew put a rescue swimmer in the water.
The rescue basket is a steel cage with floats, so a cold, worn out survivor only has to climb in and hold on while the hoist does the lifting.
One at a time, the crew winched them up through the wind.
outcome: The Coast Guard aircrew rescued both kayakers from Bellingham Bay.
title: Kayakers caught in 60 knot winds
description:
On Dec. 11, 2006, a Coast Guard helicopter crew rescued two kayakers from eight-foot swells and 50 to 60 knot winds in Bellingham Bay, Washington.
